subject: MSA & Order Form — term cycle safeguards and early-exit alignment
messages:
From: Eva Simmons <eva.simmons@jupiteranalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@jupiteranalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: MSA + Order Form: term cadence and exit mechanics

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending over the draft MSA and order form. Two quick items we need to resolve before legal will sign off on the pilot (timed launch next month):

1) Auto-renew / notice window: The MSA currently has an auto-renew with a 90-day notice. Our procurement team requires a 60-day notice at most — is Redwood willing to reduce that?

2) Termination for convenience (TFC): The Order Form doesn't include an explicit TFC right for us. We understand there are operational handback considerations; we may accept a short transition fee, but we need a clear, doable mechanism (timeline, deliverables, data return).

I've attached our internal checklist; cc'd Tom (ops) in case we need to align on the handback specifics. Can you share Redwood's recommended fallback (e.g., 60-day notice + 30-day transition & prorated refund)? Also please loop in legal so we can get redlines quickly.

Appreciate it — Eva
[Attachment: Jupiter_MSA_Checklist.pdf (42 KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Eva Simmons <eva.simmons@jupiteranalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 17:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: term cadence and exit mechanics

Hi Eva — thanks for the clear asks.

Short answer: yes, we can propose compromises. I've attached a version of the MSA with two options called out (Option A: 60-day auto-renew notice; Option B: 30-day notice with an annual commitment uplift). For TFC we've added an explicit handback schedule and a capped transition fee (equivalent to 30 days of committed fees) as a starting point.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura (legal) to confirm language and any SOW linkage for handback deliverables.
- Ben (your commercial lead) to confirm whether the 30-day capped fee is acceptable or if you need purely prorated refunds only.
- Karthik to confirm operational readiness for a pilot cutover in May assuming we lock terms this week.

I've attached: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.docx (redlines with inline comments) and the updated OrderForm_Jupiter_20270403.pdf.

If this looks directionally right, can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize wording for DocuSign?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.docx (17 KB), OrderForm_Jupiter_20270403.pdf (12 KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: term cadence and exit mechanics — legal input

Marissa / team —

I've reviewed the redlines and the two-option approach. High-level recommendations:

- Auto-renew notice: 60 days is reasonable for our hosted offering. We'll mark Option A as the default (60-day notice) and keep Option B as a commercial concession requiring a 12-month minimum commitment.

- TFC mechanics: We should include an explicit TFC clause in the Order Form that references a short, scheduled handback plan in an SOW. Proposed language: the customer may terminate for convenience with 60 days' notice; Redwood will provide a staged handback over 30 days and refund any pre-paid amounts pro rata less the capped transition fee equal to one month of committed fees. This balances customer flexibility and our operational costs.

- Data return / preservation: Add a 90-day snapshot retention after active service ends (no additional charges) and an optional extended export assistance package if the customer wants us to handle full migration (priced separately).

- Approval path: These changes are commercial-friendly but we should get an explicit sign-off from revenue operations for the capped-fee threshold for large TCVs (> $250k) — otherwise legal recommends a scaled fee.

I'll prepare a short proposed paragraph to drop into the Order Form (and mark it in the attached redline). Ben / Karthik: can one of you confirm whether we need the scaled-fee path for JUP-54812? Marissa: I'll be on the call tomorrow at 11:00 if we schedule it — otherwise I'll send the paragraph by EOD.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
General Counsel (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: inline edits in Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.docx]

From: Eva Simmons <eva.simmons@jupiteranalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@jupiteranalytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: term cadence and exit mechanics

Thanks — this is helpful and faster than expected.

Confirming Jupiter Analytics can accept the following compromise:
- Auto-renew notice shortened to 60 days (Option A).
- Contract may include a customer TFC right with 60 days' notice; Redwood to perform a 30-day staged handback. Any pre-paid fees to be refunded pro rata less a capped transition fee equal to 1 month of committed fees.

We ask only to see the precise paragraph you'll insert into the Order Form and the SOW for the handback tasks. If Laura can send that paragraph (or confirm on the call tomorrow), we should be able to get this across the finish line and circulate for signature.

Please send the DocuSign link once finalized — Tom will be the signee from our side.

Best,
Eva Simmons
Head of Procurement
Jupiter Analytics
